newsitem.title: USA: United Meridian stock plunges after drilling news.
newsitem.headline: United Meridian stock plunges after drilling news.

text.p: United Meridian Corp's stock dropped sharply on Tuesday after the company said it encountered two dry holes in drilling off the coast of western Africa.
The stock closed down seven at 43 in trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Turnover was 1.6 million shares, about 10 times the daily average.
Analysts said that Perla 1 -- the first well drilled on the company's 75 percent-owned Block D off Equatorial Guinea -- was a particular disappointment.
The well had appeared to be "right on trend" with the Zafiro field on Block B, where United Meridian has a 25 percent interest, analyst Andrew Burns of John S. Herold Inc said.
The market was counting on "continued drilling success into the 75 percent-owned block," he explained, saying it was "expecting big, big things."
The stock's big decline may have also reflected profit-taking, Burns said. Its recent high of 53-3/8 was more than three and a half times greater than its 52-year low of 15, he said.
